results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 63 aligned outline summaries state the controlling idea of their spec paragraph, in spec order; the five callouts are framing apparatus with no spec paragraph.
The independent reverse outline lists the same controlling ideas in the same order as the spec's sections and paragraphs (p01-p63).

results.draft_locus: The Tracking Plan: The Schema Nobody Can Recall ¶5
results.quote: Every event carries a **common envelope**: event ID (for de-duplication), event time and receive time, the tenant
results.finding: The outliner marked this unit as two ideas, and it is: (1) the fields of the common envelope and (2) two collection rules (facts server-side, impressions compacted not dropped). The draft itself says the rules 'follow from the table' (the core-events table of p18), not from the envelope, so nothing unifies the two halves. The spec paragraph p19 bundles both as one controlling idea; splitting them needs a spec change (a unit cannot be added by the draft).
Every unit advances its section's declared supporting claims (S1-S6) or is declared framing (intro context, roadmap, hand-off); no unit drifts off the thesis.

Each table is introduced and read (six-consumer table by p11, three-kinds table by p13, core events by p19, layer table by p23/p24, quality table by p48, storage options with the recommendation and p28, ownership matrix, definition card by p35, replay table by p38, legal table by p45, trade-offs and verticals by their lead-ins and p56); figures carry explanatory captions; quotations (Dehghani, Adevinta 2024, Aurelia 2025, Armbrust et al.) are each followed by what they show.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary, by an explicit bridge sentence (e.g. 'Owning the word starts with knowing what the platform is for', 'The tracking plan governs one input; the reference architecture below receives all of them', 'The contacts data product needs a definition its owner publishes', 'Access policy settles what data may be used') or, where a subheading opens the unit (data products, storage, verticals), by a predecessor's forward pointer and the opening claim; both flow readers followed every boundary.

Both flow readers state the declared organising principle: a problem scene, then the platform in prerequisite order along the data's path (purpose, tracking plan, architecture, data products, governed metrics, pro data, cross-brand limits, freshness and cost), then the worked Veldmark design and the book's judging sections. No section is marked unclear; Freshness and Cost was called 'somewhat arbitrary' (A) and 'partly unclear' (B) but both accepted its bridge sentence and neither lost the thread. Unexplained book-level names both readers met (Safe Deal, Yardstick, Veldmark ID, Valuo, billable lead, Common Ground) are on audience.already_knows and are not counted.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: Three Warehouses, Three Contacts ¶2
results.quote: Tradeyard and Motorvane run Snowflake, in separate accounts with separate models. Hearthly runs BigQuery. Keybridge runs Azure Synapse
results.finding: Reader A: 'That is four environments, or three if the two Snowflake accounts count as one... I re-read to work out which three were meant.' The heading and the later 'Most of that bill paid for three separate warehouses' (In Practice ¶1) say three while four engines/accounts are listed; the text never says 'three' means the three listing brands' warehouses. The order is fine; the prose leaves the count unresolved.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-b item 7 ('"Three warehouses" while four are listed... I paused to count')

results.quote: It describes no company's actual systems. Three of its layers hold **data products**, datasets a named team owns and publishes; their owners follow the rule in the next section.
results.finding: Reader A: 'Five new terms (data products, the gate, data contract, metrics layer, governed metric) arrive in four sentences'; 'It is unclear which three layers are meant until the table has been read'; the architecture table, Figure 2 and the medallion paragraph lean on data products before the next section defines them. The spec's order (architecture before data products, with one-clause glosses) is kept; the prose obscures it: the disclaimer interrupts the overview, the three layers are not named, and 'the next section' is three subsections away.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-b item 5 ('The opening paragraph of the architecture section is dense and points forward... I re-read this paragraph')

results.quote: The documented lesson from Adevinta Spain's contracts, Vinted's generated tracking code and Adevinta Benelux's metric monitoring, Artemis (described under governed metrics), is the same
results.finding: Reader A: 'This cites as evidence something the reader has not yet seen... I stopped to check whether I had missed it.' The quality claim leans on Artemis, which is described only two sections later (p40). The prose can make the claim without depending on unseen evidence.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-b item 6 ('Artemis is cited as evidence before it is described')

results.draft_locus: Governed Metrics: One Definition of a Contact ¶5
results.quote: The week began on Monday 8 March, the day after Femke listed her bike, so the team replayed the bike's first 24 hours with it.
results.finding: Reader A: 'If the bike was listed on Sunday 7 March, most of its first 24 hours fall before the replayed week. The "so" does not follow, and I re-read the sentence twice'; A also could not tell why the Golf's dangling fraud-review clause is there. The 'so' asserts a causal link that does not hold, the bike's 24-hour window is not stated, and the April Golf example (outside the replayed week) runs on in the same paragraph. Prose problem; the spec's content is followable if stated plainly.
results.corroborated_by: reader-flow-b item 8 ('The replay dates... I re-read this twice'; the bike's window and the Golf outside the week)

results.quote: Part VI priced, billed and tested against contact counts, and [[web-and-seo-architecture]] steered Tradeyard on organic contacts; this chapter makes "contact" mean the same thing in every brand.
results.finding: Reader A: 'This sentence interrupts the "opposite route" argument between "what a listing marketplace needs to know" and "It works back to the contracts". I lost the line of the paragraph and re-read it.' One reader only.

results.draft_locus: The Tracking Plan: The Schema Nobody Can Recall ¶5
results.quote: This one rule removed the largest disagreement between Veldmark's brands, because clients lose events to ad blockers, crashes and missing consent, while servers do not.
results.finding: Reader A: 'This appears in the general tracking-plan section, before the chapter has shown Veldmark adopting the rule. It reads as a small time jump.' One reader only.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: Three Warehouses, Three Contacts ¶3
results.quote: Tradeyard's dashboard counts **52 contacts** for it, because it counts buyer messages.
results.finding: Reader A: the table just above says Tradeyard counts 'Every message a buyer sends, plus every phone-number reveal'; 'I paused over whether phone reveals were part of the 52.' One reader only.

results.draft_locus: What a Marketplace Data Platform Is For ¶6
results.quote: CDC should be temporary in the data platform too.
results.finding: Reader B: 'the "too" points to an argument from another chapter that is only cited at the end of the paragraph.' One reader only; the referent arrives in the same paragraph.

Every term on audience.does_not_know is given at or before its first use in the body: data platform (p09), tracking plan (p15), common envelope (p19), data contract, data product and metrics layer (one-clause glosses in p23, full definitions in p25, p29, p33), governed metric (p33, previewed in the intro's framing), qualified contact (card, p34), pro data product (p41), lakehouse and open table formats Iceberg/Delta Lake (p27), medallion (p24, read as bronze/silver/gold), data mesh (p29), quarantine tables (layer table and p25), ePrivacy Art. 5(3) and purpose limitation (p20, sharing table), controller boundaries (sharing table). The flow readers' term complaints concern book-level names on already_knows (Safe Deal, Yardstick, Veldmark ID, Valuo, billable lead) or the strangler pattern, part of an architect's baseline; the early use of 'data products' in the architecture is recorded under flow_is_followable.

The intro opens with a direct, disputable statement ('Most marketplace data platforms are built backwards'), bridges to the topic, states the four contracts and the technology-after-contracts claim, and gives a roadmap; no dictionary, throat-clearing or 'in this chapter we will' opening.

The conclusion does not merely restate sections or open with 'in conclusion'; it synthesises (contracts, not engines, answered the question), gives a course of action and hands off to experimentation.

p62 states what the contracts achieved (one number for Femke's bike wherever it is read, facts rather than only data) and the first move; p63 answers the so-what: comparable measurement is what lets the group ask whether a change caused an effect.

'Henrik's question was answered by contracts' and 'Femke's bike now counts 13 wherever it is read: the platform holds facts, not only data' call back to the scene's board question and to the opening's 'a great deal of data and very few facts'.

The cold intro reader reconstructed every roadmap promise in order (board question, purpose, tracking plan, architecture with quality controls, data products, governed metrics, pro data, cross-brand sharing, freshness and cost, Common Ground, trade-offs, verticals, failure modes, Chief Architect's view, questions) and the evidence kinds; the body keeps that order.

The opening-only reader predicted the expected themes (conflicting definitions across warehouses, tracking plan as schema, governed liquidity metrics, federated ownership on one substrate with purpose-bound access), the expected section order and all four evidence kinds (named classifieds/e-commerce companies, data-mesh and lakehouse literature, EU law, fictional Veldmark).

Using only the chapter, the reader built a governed qualified-contact metric with owner and steward, written definition, single computation in the metrics layer and version, counted once per buyer and listing at server-side delivery, with fraud excluded by the 72-hour restatement, served to board pack, dealer reports and experiments, legacy definitions labeled side by side for a quarter, and the bike counting 13; and refused the subsidiary request through purpose-tagged, closed-by-default access policy with Keybridge's data excluded and its isolation reviewed independently. Matches the expected answer.
